Deployments/pods observed in namespace `shop`:

tool_input.content:
## Symptom
KubePodCrashLooping alert for deployment `api` in namespace `shop` (cluster aurora-lab). `kubectl get pods` shows api pods 1/2 Ready, STATUS OOMKilled, restarting every ~15-20s. The main `api` container itself stays Ready:True/0 restarts — only the second container is crash-looping, so top-level pod STATUS can be misleading at a glance.

## Root cause
Deployment `api` revision 2 added a `log-shipper` sidecar container:
```python
buf = bytearray(40*1024*1024)  # ~40MiB immediately on startup
while True: time.sleep(5)
```
with `resources.limits.memory: 16Mi` — ~2.5x too small for its own first allocation. Kubelet OOMKills it (exit 137) every restart, kubelet backs off (BackOff events), pod never reaches ContainersReady, Deployment reports `unavailableReplicas`/MinimumReplicasUnavailable.

Revision 1 ReplicaSet (`api-f64486c4c` in the 2026-10-02 incident) had only the single `api` container — confirms the sidecar was newly introduced in the rollout that triggered the alert.

## How to apply / diagnose next time
1. `kubectl get pods -n shop` — check RESTARTS and READY x/y; x<y with OOMKilled on one container is the signature.
2. `kubectl describe pod <pod> -n shop` — check each container's `State`/`Last State`, `Reason: OOMKilled`, `Limits.memory` vs what the container's own command/log says it allocates.
3. `kubectl logs <pod> -c <sidecar>` — look for allocation-size hints in startup logs.
4. Compare current ReplicaSet's pod spec against the previous (still-alive, lower-replica) ReplicaSet to see what container/config was added — `deployment.kubernetes.io/revision` annotation marks the rollout.
5. Fix: raise the sidecar's memory limit to safely exceed its real usage, or roll back to the prior revision if the sidecar isn't essential yet.

## Distinguish from worker/BATCH_SIZE OOM pattern
This is a different mechanism than the `shop/worker` BATCH_SIZE OOMKill (see postmortem entries) — that one is a single-container deployment whose env var controls allocation size. This one is a newly-added sidecar container with a limit that was never sized to its own workload. Don't assume BATCH_SIZE is involved just because it's the same namespace/cluster.
tool_input.description: shop/api deployment revision 2 added a log-shipper sidecar container that allocates 40MB buffer on startup against a 16Mi memory limit, causing continuous OOMKill/CrashLoopBackOff on that container while the main api container stays healthy.

Current state (kubectl get pods -n shop): api-7d4b6f6f7d-m29sh and api-7d4b6f6f7d-ng552 are 1/2 Ready, STATUS=OOMKilled, RESTARTS=3 at 55-57s ago — actively crash-looping right now. All other shop pods (frontend, worker, redis, loadgen) are 1/1 or 2/2 Ready with 0 restarts.
kubectl describe pod api-7d4b6f6f7d-m29sh: Two containers in the pod:
   - api — Running, Ready: True, Restart Count: 0 (healthy, 128Mi limit).
   - log-shipper (new sidecar) — State: Terminated, Reason: OOMKilled, Exit Code: 137, Restart Count: 3, memory Limit: 16Mi. Command: buf=bytearray(4010241024) executed immediately on start.
kubectl logs ... -c log-shipper: "log-shipper: buffering 40 MB before first flush" — confirms the container allocates ~40MiB instantly, 2.5x over its 16Mi limit, guaranteeing OOMKill on every start.
Deployment diff (kubectl get deployment api -o yaml vs old RS): Current deployment is revision 2 (deployment.kubernetes.io/revision: "2"). The prior ReplicaSet api-f64486c4c (revision 1, still alive, 1/1 Ready, 0 restarts) has only the single api container — no log-shipper. Revision 2 added the log-shipper sidecar with the undersized memory limit.
Deployment status: replicas: 3, readyReplicas: 1, unavailableReplicas: 2, condition Deployment does not have minimum availability — matches the alert's "pods restarting" symptom at the deployment level.
Ruled out: Node pressure (all 3 nodes Ready, other pods on same nodes stable) and Redis/app-level failure (the api container itself is healthy, Ready=True, 0 restarts, REDIS_HOST resolves to a running redis pod).

Root Cause — CONFIRMED
A rollout to revision 2 of the shop/api Deployment added a log-shipper sidecar container whose startup code immediately allocates a 40MiB in-memory buffer, but the container's memory limit was set to only 16Mi. The kubelet OOMKills it (exit 137) within seconds of every restart,

Conclusion: CONFIRMED root cause.

The shop/api deployment's rollout to revision 2 added a log-shipper sidecar container that allocates a 40MiB buffer on startup against only a 16Mi memory limit, causing it to OOMKill (exit 137) immediately and repeatedly, which keeps the api pods in CrashLoopBackOff/1/2 Ready and the Deployment below minimum availability. The primary api application container is healthy and unaffected (Ready: True, 0 restarts) — the user-facing API itself is likely still serving traffic through the one fully-available pod, but the Deployment can't reach its desired replica count, which is what's firing the alert.

Recommended fix (validated feasible, but blocked by read-only policy — needs an engineer with write access):
Preferred: Raise log-shipper's memory limit to ≥64Mi to accommodate its 40MiB allocation + Python overhead.
Fallback: Roll back to revision 1 (api-f64486c4c), which has no sidecar and is confirmed currently healthy (1/1 Ready).

Saved this failure pattern to memory (learned/shop/api CrashLoop - log-shipper sidecar OOM (rev2 rollout)) for future recurrence detection, and noted it's distinct from the previously-documented shop/worker BATCH_SIZE OOM pattern.
